data.title: ‘It Makes Sense,’ Says Investor as Alphabet Stock Enters Dangerous Territory
data.description:
Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) held up well during Thursday’s market meltdown, slipping just 2.2% while the Nasdaq plunged 5.5%. But zoom out, and Google’s parent has lost 18% of its value over the past month, while its nearly 10% year-to-date retreat puts it well behind the broader tech index.

Much of Alphabet’s trouble began with its disappointing third-quarter earnings, which exposed the growing financial burden of its AI expansion. Although revenue climbed 25%, profits missed expectations, massive infrastructure investments pushed free cash flow into negative territory, and additional borrowing raised concerns about future profitability. Meanwhile, slower growth in Google’s advertising operations has left investors wondering whether its traditional money-making engine can support such expensive technological investments.

One investor certainly isn’t losing sleep over Alphabet’s falling share price. Known as Bears of Wall Street (BWS), he has maintained a bearish position since the summer, long before the latest earnings disappointment. With his earlier warning now looking well-timed, BWS believes further losses could await those hoping for a recovery.

“We believe that it makes perfect sense to stick with our Sell rating for Alphabet,” BWS noted. Well, Bears of Wall Street indeed.

The financial figures provide some context for his concerns, particularly regarding the scale of ongoing investment commitments. Capital expenditures reached $51.4 billion during Q3, contributing to negative free cash flow totaling $9.1 billion. Alphabet also maintained its annual spending forecast of $195 billion to $205 billion, with further increases anticipated throughout 2027.

Financing those obligations presents another challenge, especially considering the company’s growing reliance on external funding sources. Long-term debt reached $125.1 billion by September, compared with $46.5 billion at December’s close. Quarterly interest expenses consequently climbed to $967 million from $143 million one year earlier, potentially limiting the benefits of continued sales expansion.

Meanwhile, Google’s search division generated $63.4 billion in quarterly revenue, representing 12% annual growth versus 17% during the preceding period. BWS worries that consumers migrating toward conversational assistants could weaken advertising profitability, particularly as monetization within newer AI-powered features remains less developed.

Furthermore, despite the recent selloff, the investor sees little comfort in Alphabet’s current valuation, noting: “All of those risks make us believe that Alphabet remains overvalued even at the current price.”

His discounted cash flow analysis assigns the company an estimated intrinsic value of $171.98 per share, about 39% below Thursday’s closing price.

Overall, with borrowing costs rising and traditional advertising facing technological competition, his bearish outlook suggests the latest retreat may be only the beginning. (To watch Bears of Wall Street’s track record, click here)

data.title: Nvidia or Broadcom: Cathie Wood Buys $45.9M of One AI Stock, Sells $119.7M of the Other
data.description:
Thursday brought another brutal session for semiconductor investors, with Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) tumbling about 9% and slipping into negative territory for 2026. The stock now sits around 2% lower year-to-date, erasing earlier gains as the market reconsiders the outlook for AI infrastructure spending. Much of the anxiety follows the Democrats’ sweeping midterm election victory, which has raised concerns about stricter oversight of data-center construction and potential delays to future projects. Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) also suffered a steep setback, losing 10.5% during Thursday’s session and extending its 2026 losses to about 16%.

Both companies benefit from tech customers investing heavily in computing capacity, leaving their valuations exposed whenever confidence in those spending plans weakens.

However, recent market turbulence has prompted Cathie Wood to favor one semiconductor leader over the other. The ARK Invest founder bought Thursday’s dip in NVDA, purchasing 252,592 shares through her firm’s funds, worth $45.9 million at current prices. Broadcom’s selloff apparently looked less appealing, with Wood’s funds selling 410,559 shares valued at $119.7 million.

Nvidia’s Stock Takes a Hit, but Analysts See Huge Upside

Nvidia’s latest plunge reflects anxiety that future data-center development could proceed more slowly than previously anticipated, particularly following the Democrats’ midterm election victories. Political resistance to large facilities has grown amid complaints about electricity bills, water usage, and pressure on local infrastructure. Any resulting project delays could postpone purchases of advanced graphics processors, potentially affecting revenue expectations despite healthy underlying demand.

Investors also worry whether hyperscalers can maintain their massive capital expenditure programs without generating stronger returns from AI services. For Nvidia, whose chips power much of today’s model training and inference activity, even modest changes in customer investment schedules can unsettle markets. Still, demand for next-generation computing hardware remains an important counterweight to fears surrounding near-term volatility.

Yet, Wood’s decision to buy Nvidia on Thursday’s dip echoes Wall Street’s message to investors: Don’t panic. All 33 covering analysts recommend buying the stock, giving it a unanimous Strong Buy consensus rating. The average 12-month price target stands at $322.50, implying 77% upside from Thursday’s closing price. (See NVDA stock forecast)

Cathie Wood Sells Broadcom, but Wall Street Sees 80% Upside

Wood’s decision to sell Broadcom comes at an interesting time, particularly following recent developments involving AI startup Anthropic. The chipmaker is involved in a $63 billion financing arrangement backed by Bank of America, Blackstone, Citi, and Morgan Stanley, supporting purchases of its AI accelerators and networking equipment for Anthropic.

Yet, the same spending concerns now threatening its rival also apply to Broadcom, particularly if planned construction projects face political obstacles. Thursday’s heavy selling suggests investors are reconsidering how much future chip demand has already been incorporated into market valuations. Continued orders for custom accelerators may support longer-term growth, although sentiment could remain volatile.

Analysts remain enthusiastic, with 29 Buy recommendations and one Hold supporting Broadcom’s bullish consensus. The average price target of $523.72 indicates about 80% potential upside from Thursday’s closing price, slightly exceeding Nvidia’s projected return. Wood may prefer the latter today, but Wall Street still sees significant room for both stocks to recover. (See AVGO stock forecast)

data.title: ‘Watch Your Step,’ Says Investor About Micron Stock
data.description:
The selloff in memory chip stocks has gone from bad to worse, with Micron (NASDAQ:MU) plunging 17% during Thursday’s session and losing nearly 30% of its value over the past week. Investors are growing nervous about the sustainability of massive AI infrastructure spending, particularly following the Democrats’ midterm election victory, which has raised concerns about potential restrictions on data-center construction.

Adding to Wall Street’s worries, Qualcomm’s disappointing quarterly results have raised doubts about smartphone demand, while uncertainty surrounding future memory prices is weighing on semiconductor manufacturers. With Micron shares now trading far below their recent highs, bargain hunters might see an opportunity to purchase the stock at a steep discount.

However, investor David Desjardins believes buying into this weakness could prove costly, maintaining his Strong Sell rating despite the recent collapse. Having warned about Micron’s valuation back in July, he remains convinced that the industry’s remarkable profitability may ultimately create serious problems for those purchasing shares today.

Desjardins is particularly concerned about what happens after 2028, when spending by leading tech companies could begin slowing just as semiconductor manufacturers bring additional factories online. Although he anticipates tremendous earnings during the next two fiscal years, his bearish outlook reflects fears that investors are overlooking the consequences of excessive production capacity.

“The memory shortages of today could contain the very seed of the oversupply of tomorrow,” Desjardins opined.

One reason for his caution involves Oracle, whose capital expenditures are expected to peak during fiscal 2027 and 2028 before falling in fiscal 2029. That anticipated reduction could offer an early indication of how other hyperscalers might eventually scale back their infrastructure budgets.

Desjardins expects total spending among these customers to reach $1.3 trillion by 2028, supporting robust demand for high-bandwidth memory throughout that period. However, the investor anticipates a turning point thereafter, when financing constraints and weaker investment growth could undermine the favorable conditions currently benefiting Micron.

Meanwhile, semiconductor manufacturers are preparing to expand output through multibillion-dollar construction projects, creating another potential threat to future pricing. Micron’s Idaho facilities are scheduled to begin contributing additional supply in 2027 and 2028, followed by its first New York factory in 2030.

Samsung Electronics and SK hynix are pursuing similarly extensive expansion plans, raising the possibility that global production could accelerate precisely when customer purchases begin losing momentum. Such an outcome would expose memory suppliers to falling selling prices, potentially reversing the earnings boom that currently makes their stocks appear so inexpensive.

Desjardins also warns against interpreting Micron’s low earnings multiple as proof that investors have discovered a bargain. Based on his experience with mining, energy, and shipping investments, the investor believes seemingly cheap cyclical companies can become expensive purchases when their profits approach unsustainable levels.

“Watch your step, and beware of deeply cyclical stocks trading at single-digit valuation multiples,” Desjardins summed up. (To watch Desjardins’ track record, click here)

Wall Street, however, sees Micron’s prospects far more favorably than Desjardins, with analysts maintaining a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 28 Buys and just one Hold. The average price target of $1,621.67 suggests a whopping 147% upside from Thursday’s closing price. (See MU stock forecast)
